ai.description: *Micrixalus candidus* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and a distinctive white patch on the cheeks. It exhibits characteristic foot-flagging behavior and possesses a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus candidus* is best distinguished by the distinct, stark white patch covering its entire cheek, which contrasts sharply against its darker, mottled brown body.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus candidus* inhabits shaded, rocky stream beds within evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The White-Cheeked Dancing Frog performs "foot-flagging," a unique behavioral display where males extend and wave their hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus candidus* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in subterranean nests within stream beds, where larvae develop hidden in the gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus candidus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The White-Cheeked Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, short, and repetitive "tink" sound, typically heard near fast-flowing, rocky streams in Western Ghats forests.
